content: In the unborn expanse of the dharmadhātu,Dwells the Mother, the Noble Lady, Goddess Tārā.She who bestows happiness upon all sentient beings,I pray, protect me from every fear!Without realizing that one’s own nature is the dharmakāya,The mind falls under the power of the afflictions;To the mother-beings wandering in saṃsāra,O Mother Goddess, I pray that you protect them.Without the Dharma truly arising within one's stream of being,Following after conventional words,And deceived by inferior philosophical tenets,May the Goddess, the Perfect Mother, protect us.One's own mind is difficult to realize;Without having meditated after seeing it,For those distracted by unwholesome activities,I pray to the Goddess of Mindfulness, the Mother, to protect them.Within the mind, the self-arisen non-dual primordial wisdom,By the habitual tendencies of dualistic grasping,No matter what they do, those who are bound—I pray that the Goddess of non-dual wisdom may protect us.Although we abide within the ultimate reality,Because we do not understand the dependent origination of cause and effect,And are deluded regarding the nature of all that can be known,I pray that the Mother, the Goddess of Omniscience, may protect us.Characterized by the nature of space, free from conceptual elaboration,Inseparable from all that exists—To those of us who are still but trainee individuals,O Mother, the Perfect Buddha, I pray that you grant protection.This prayer, known as the "Seven Protections," was offered by the King of Dharma of the three realms, the Victorious Drigungpa, Kyobpa Rje 'Jig-rten-gsum-gyi-mgon-po, when he beheld the seven faces of the Noble Tara in the E-chung cave; it is renowned for its immense blessings.
